messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: hosted-runtime eu-west-1 cluster: KV cache memory spike + multiple OOMs detected on runtime-pool-7. Alerts at 4135791999. Escalating to on-call.

alex: on it, seeing a bunch of longprompt sessions hammering the prefix KV. Mem use at ~96-99% on two nodes, OOMs on one.

mei: thanks alex — any customer-facing errors?

ops-jordan: Grafana shows 502s spiking for the hosted-api route /v1/chat/generate starting 3m ago. Error rate ~3.8%, tail latency jump.

customer-success-anya: we've received one support ticket from a customer reporting repeated failures for long chat sessions. No PII.

alex: root cause suspicion: runaway context windows with continuous batching + prefetch enabled. Prefetch logic is reusing large prefixes and creating huge kvmaps per session. Looks like a growth loop when session tokens > 25k.

sre-lead-raj: good summary. Priority: prevent more OOMs and reduce customer impact. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) apply runtime flag to cap per-session prefetched_kv entries to 128, 2) enable short-circuit for requests with input_length > 30k to bypass KV prefetch, 3) throttle batch size for hosted-runtime to force smaller per-request memory.

alex: agree. I can push the bypass flag as a hotpatch to host pool-7. Will do a targeted canary on 1 host first.

mei: please also add a traffic policy to route heavy sessions to a lower-priority capacity tier (dedicated-burst) if available. We don't want blast radius on the main pool.

ops-jordan: adding a temporary session-level limiter via envoy header rewrite is possible — I can inject header X-Redwood-Session-Preload-Limit:128 for /v1/chat/generate for sessions flagged as long.

alex: performing hotpatch now. Command: 
```
# hotpatch: limit per-session prefetch
./hotpatch_ctl apply --pool hosted-runtime-eu-west-1 --canary 1 --flag kv_prefetch_max_per_session=128 --flag kv_prefetch_bypass_for_input_gt=30000
```

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy on hosted-runtime-eu-west-1 host runtime-7-03. Rolling window: 2m.

monitoring-bot: canary metrics streaming -> https://grafana/redwood/d/kvcache/hosted-runtime-eu-west-1 (canary host: runtime-7-03)

alex: canary up, injecting heavy test session (30k token replay). Observing memory and kvmap size.

mei: ping when you see stabilization or regression.

alex: after ~90s canary host mem dropped from 98% -> 62% with flagged behavior. No OOM on the canary. Prefetch entries per session dropped to ~90.

ops-jordan: started envoy header injection for flagged sessions on edge nodes. Will monitor 1m windows.

customer-success-anya: letting the affected customer know we applied mitigations; they asked for ETA to full rollout. I told them it's in canary and we'll update in 15m if stable.

sre-lead-raj: proceed to roll canary to 30% of hosts in the pool. Keep the bypass flag active. Also reduce continuous batch max tokens to 4096 for hosted pool to limit per-batch KV footprint.

alex: rolling to 30% now: 
```
./hotpatch_ctl roll --pool hosted-runtime-eu-west-1 --pct 30 --flags kv_prefetch_max_per_session=128,kv_prefetch_bypass_for_input_gt=30000,continuous_batch_max_tokens=4096
```

deploy-bot: rolling to 30% - ETA 4m.

monitoring-bot: cluster-level mem usage trending down. Error rate back to ~0.8% within 6m of canary.

ops-jordan: noticed one host with slow eviction (disk-backed swap) — manually restarted the runtime process on runtime-7-11 to clear transient state. No customer sessions lost; connections drained gracefully.

alex: after restarts and roll, mem stable ~48-65% across pool. No further OOMs in the last 10m.

customer-success-anya: customer confirmed they can proceed and errors reduced. They're going to retest their long-session flows and will update if anything flares.

sre-lead-raj: good. Next steps: (1) keep the hotpatch for 24 hours, (2) create a follow-up RFC to make long-input bypass permanent with safety thresholds, (3) instrument a new metric: prefetched_kv_entries_per_session_90p and session_input_token_histogram, (4) schedule an infra postmortem if we see recurrence.

mei: I captured the runbook change: add prefetch caps and a sacrificial short-circuit for >30k tokens. Also adding an alert: if average prefetched_kv_entries_per_session > 512 for 5m, page SRE.

alex: logging actions in incident tracker (#INC-4135792001). Adding links: runbook diff: https://git.redwood/runbooks/kv-prefetch/compare/patch-413579, grafana dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/kvcache/hosted-runtime-eu-west-1

ops-jordan: starting to rollback the envoy header injection after roll is stable — leaving the runtime flags active until tomorrow morning.

monitoring-bot: no new OOMs in 20m. CPU and token throughput nominal.

mei: handing off to morning on-call @mei (on rotation) — please keep hotpatch and monitor for 6 hours, then coordinate staged revert to a long-term config once the RFC lands.

alex: adding checklist for handoff: 1) track prefetched_kv_entries_per_session_90p, 2) watch for spike in tail latency after continuous_batch_max_tokens change, 3) be ready to set kv_prefetch_max_per_session=64 if mem reheats.

customer-success-anya: I'll follow up with the customer in 2h with status and next steps.

sre-lead-raj: incident marked as mitigated for now. We'll call it MONITORING. Re-open if OOMs resume. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
